summary: notebook-auto-prune.sh drop-oldest selection misfires when a heading embeds a bare numeric commit hash after its real ISO timestamp -- the hash gets misread as a bogus far-future date, corrupting which section is chosen as oldest

payload.mechanism: nso_ts_key() in scripts/agents-flow/lib/notebook-section-direction.sh:71-81 extracts a timestamp via `grep -oE '[0-9]{4}-?[0-9]{2}-?[0-9]{2}(T...Z)?' | tail -1` -- ANY run of >=8 digits that happens to fall into a YYYY-MM-DD shape matches, with no anchoring to require the T...Z time suffix and no distinction between 'the section's real timestamp' and 'any other digit run on the same heading line.' `tail -1` always prefers the LAST match on the line, so a heading of the form '## cycle-705 - 2026-08-14T01:33:11Z - ... (commit `761988143`)' extracts the real timestamp '2026-08-14T01:33:11Z' but is vulnerable the moment a second qualifying digit run (any embedded commit SHA/PR number/etc that happens to start with an 8-digit date-shaped prefix) appears AFTER the real timestamp in the same heading -- the parser silently keys off the hash instead.
payload.independently_confirmed: router re-derived by hand against the live regex+heading pair in docs/agent-memory/notebooks/qa.md:15 ('## cycle-705 ... commit `761988143`'): grep -oE against that exact string returns '2026-08-14' then '76198814' as two separate matches (the commit hash's leading 8 digits alone satisfy the YYYY-MM-DD shape); `tail -1` picks '76198814', zero-padded to '76198814000000000' -- a sort key ~2.4 million years in the future relative to any real section. Confirmed this IS a live, reachable code path, not a hypothetical -- did not independently reproduce a live mis-drop of cycle-708 (qa.md currently holds only 2 sections, cycle-709 and cycle-705, 29 lines total, nowhere near cap -- no prune actually fired this tick, so cycle-708's absence could not be attributed to this bug specifically vs. an earlier unrelated drop; QA's own agent (aa95e653b09a1880f) reported reproducing the misselection directly via nso_sections_with_ts against reconstructed pre-hook content, which router did not re-run).
payload.distinct_from_existing_board_rows: grepped orch-state.json task_board for related rows before filing (avoid duplicate mint): FIX-NOTEBOOK-PRUNE-HEADING-LEVEL-MISMATCH, FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTO-PRUNE-STALENESS-GUARD, FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-ROLLING-SECTIONS-BYTE-COUNTED-BUT-UNDROPPABLE, and FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-REGEX-HEADING-MISMATCH (status=REVIEW, next_agent=qa, developer's 2026-07-12 fix widened the heading regex to cover multiple timestamp FORMATS and fixed a 'drops newest not oldest' sort-direction defect -- a different mechanism, sort direction vs. false-positive timestamp extraction). None of the four cover 'a non-timestamp digit run on the same heading line gets misparsed as a timestamp.' This also is not the same shape as the two entries already in feedback_auditor_cappressure_trim_partially_truncates_retained_section.md (partial truncation of a byte-identical retained section) or the sentinel-key processed signal from 2026-08-07 (dated section always wins as MIN_KEY against sentinel-keyed rolling sections) -- this is a THIRD distinct nso_ts_key()/prune-selection defect family.
payload.recommended_fix_direction: anchor the regex so a bare digit run without the T...Z time-suffix is not eligible as a timestamp candidate at all (require the full ISO shape, not just the date prefix), and/or restrict extraction to a fixed position in the heading template (immediately after the '## cycle-NNN Β· ' prefix) rather than scanning the whole line with tail -1. Either change independently closes this path without touching the FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-REGEX-HEADING-MISMATCH fix already in flight.
